Command: Do not eat an animal found dead
Summary: An animal that dies of itself, not slaughtered, may not be eaten by Israel; it may be given to the stranger, but Israel, as a holy people, shall not eat it.
Commandment: Do not eat any animal found dead of itself.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The rule kept Israel from eating carrion, whose blood was not properly shed and whose death was unwitnessed. The New Testament records these food distinctions set aside (Mark 7:19; Acts 10).
Purpose: To mark Israel's table as distinct (Leviticus 11). The New Testament records the distinctions set aside: Jesus declares all foods clean (Mark 7:19) and Peter's vision confirms it (Acts 10).
